0.long_answer: Bevacizumab is a recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody that was initially approved in the US in 2004 for the treatment of several types of cancer, primarily due to its ability to inhibit angiogenesis by blocking VEGF-A. Recent studies have demonstrated that bevacizumab can also be effective in patients with Neurofibromatosis type II, where it has been shown to reduce tumor growth—particularly in vestibular schwannomas—and improve hearing outcomes. This dual benefit, stemming from its anti-angiogenic properties, makes it a notable treatment option for addressing both tumor control and hearing improvement in individuals affected by Neurofibromatosis type II.
